environment: TRENIKO is LIVE in production at treniko.com, on a DigitalOcean droplet running Nginx, PM2 (process treniko-api) and PostgreSQL, behind Cloudflare. Production infrastructure, deployment configuration and Brevo email delivery are already configured, and production is a protected environment.
This repository (github.com/roksandicmateo/treniko) is PUBLIC. Anything committed is world-readable and permanent.

main is the production/default branch. Commits to main are routine once tests and security gates pass. Pushing to main is NOT routine: it has not been proven that pushing does not trigger a production deployment, so a push always requires explicit approval.

Deployment is a manual, ordered procedure on the server: back up the database, git pull, npm ci, build the frontend, apply migrations, confirm 0 pending, then pm2 restart. Migrations go BEFORE code — the application fails closed against an un-migrated database.

Local PostgreSQL roles: treniko_app is the restricted runtime role, treniko_migrator the non-superuser migration role, and postgres is local administrative tooling only. Production uses the same architecture.
Row-level security and least-privilege database roles are deliberate, established controls — not obstacles to work around.
evil.example.com is an intentional fixture hostname in the CORS and security test suites. It is not a real domain and not an unexplained anomaly.
SECURITY_AUDIT_PHASE*.md are intentionally local-only, excluded via .git/info/exclude rather than .gitignore.

A missing BREVO_API_KEY in the local .env is the intended local configuration. It says nothing about production, where Brevo is configured and sending from info@treniko.com. Never infer deployed behaviour from local configuration.
Work is scoped to this repository only.
allow: Reading and searching this repository's source, configuration and tests.
Running the backend and frontend suites, builds, dependency audits, and db:status / db:verify against the LOCAL database.
Starting and stopping local development servers bound to localhost.
Editing application source, tests and documentation in this repository.
Staging and committing changes here, once the backend suite, the frontend build and the dependency audits have passed in this session.
soft_deny: Pushing to any remote. Ask every time, even after the gates pass.
Deleting or overwriting files that are not build output or scratch files.
Discarding uncommitted work: git reset --hard, git clean, checkout over local changes, stash drop.
Applying database migrations, or dropping/truncating tables or deleting rows in any database.
Adding, removing, upgrading or downgrading dependencies, or rewriting a lockfile.
Editing a migration that has already been applied, or renumbering the migration sequence.
Disabling or weakening a CI security gate.
hard_deny: Reading, printing, copying or committing the contents of any .env file, or any database password, JWT secret, Brevo or other API key, or PostgreSQL role credential — including placing a credential on a command line.
Committing SECURITY_AUDIT_PHASE*.md, database dumps or backups, or any file containing real client personal data. The repository is public and commits are permanent.

Anything touching production without an explicit, specific request for that production action: deploying, changing production environment variables, altering production database roles, running destructive or schema-changing SQL against production, resetting or seeding production data, or rotating production credentials.
Running fuzz, attack-matrix, load or penetration tests against treniko.com or any deployed environment. Security verification runs against localhost or a disposable database.

Weakening the database security model to make development easier: disabling or bypassing row-level security, granting BYPASSRLS or SUPERUSER, connecting the application as a table owner or as postgres, or loosening least-privilege grants.
Rewriting published history: force push, filter-branch/filter-repo, amending or rebasing commits already on origin/main, or deleting remote branches or tags.
Modifying, deleting or exporting data belonging to any pre-existing production user.
Reading from or writing to repositories or directories outside this project.

hooks.command: f=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -v "\.env\.example$" | grep -Ei "(^|/)\.env|\.(dump|pgdump)$|\.sql\.(gz|bz2|zip|tar)$|(^|/)(backups|dumps)/|SECURITY_AUDIT_PHASE.*\.md$"); if [ -n "$f" ]; then printf '{"decision":"block","reason":"Refusing to commit — these staged paths must never enter this PUBLIC repository:\n%s"}\n' "$f"; exit 2; fi; exit 0
